doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

chapter: De De's career and trumpet players
title: Kid Rene and Buddy Petit compared
summary: De De says Kid Rene was his favorite, a fast-fingered high-range player of a better class of music, while Buddy Petit played ballhouse blues.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Of all the trumpet players you've heard, the older men here from around New Orleans, who was your favorite? Rene.
What style did he play? You might tell us, I heard him once.

Well, almost the same style I have. I've taken his style almost completely. In other words, we called fast fingerling trumpets, loud. Yeah. Phraises, you know, on the trumpet. Yeah, he was known for that. Did he have a big range?
Somebody told me he played pretty high too. Did he play?
How did he compare with Buddy Petit in this style? I never heard Buddy Petit at all and I only heard Kid Rene.

What would we call, what you say, well, what we call it here, Ballhouse. Buddy was more well, Ballhouse. In other words, he was rated higher class than the music line, you understand? Rene was. In other words, he played a better class of music.
Yeah, and Buddy played most of this blues stuff and all, more than Rene did, you know? Yeah. That's the difference in them two.
